content.title: About
content.content: Barfi (also spelled burfi) is a traditional Indian confection made from milk, sugar, and aromatic additives, often enriched with nuts, dried fruits, or spices. It is traditionally prepared by slowly reducing milk to a thick paste, then incorporating flavorings and shaping the mixture into small squares or rounds.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Barfi is commonly made at home, but it is also sold in Indian sweet shops and market stalls.
There are many flavor variations: classic cardamom, pistachio, coconut, mango, and even chocolate.
The name “burfi” derives from the Persian word “burf,” meaning “sweet.”
In some regions, barfi is served as tiny cubes dusted with powdered sugar.
The dessert is a staple at celebrations such as weddings and religious festivals.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The milk base provides a notable amount of calcium, essential for bone health.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Milk protein contributes to muscle maintenance.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Sugar and milk deliver quick energy, useful during periods of high physical activity.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Milk supplies riboflavin (B2) and B12, supporting metabolic processes.

items.title: Antioxidant spices
items.content: Cardamom, saffron, and cloves, often added to barfi, have antioxidant properties.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Barfi is very sweet, so people with diabetes or those watching their weight should limit intake.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The dairy base can cause discomfort for individuals who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Nut allergies
items.content: Varieties containing nuts (pistachios, almonds) may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Barfi is calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended to avoid over‑consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Barfi is served in small bite‑size pieces, often dusted with powdered sugar. It can be enjoyed on its own, added to fruit salads, used as a filling for sweet rolls, or paired with tea.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store barfi in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep it refrigerated, where it stays fresh for up to 2 weeks. Discard if it develops a sour smell or visible mold.

cabbage-green-cooked-no-added-fat.title: Cabbage, green, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Green cabbage is a leafy cruciferous vegetable widely used in cooking. When boiled without added fat it retains most of its vitamins, minerals, and a mild, tender flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cabbage is one of the oldest cultivated plants, with cultivation dating back over 5,000 years.
There are more than 200 cabbage varieties, including Savoy, kale, and Brussels sprouts.
Cabbage leaves contain glucosinolates, compounds that may help protect against cancer.
It features in traditional dishes worldwide: sauerkraut in Germany, kimchi in Korea, coleslaw in the United States.
Boiling in salted water helps preserve its bright green color thanks to chlorophyll.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: A serving of cooked green cabbage provides over 100 % of the daily vitamin C requirement, supporting immunity and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Source of vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health; cabbage supplies a large portion of the daily need.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Minerals: potassium and calcium
items.content: Potassium supports fluid balance, while calcium contributes to strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Cooked cabbage without fat contains about 25 kcal per 100 g, making it an excellent choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Cabbage contains raffinose, which can cause gas in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Interaction with blood thinners
items.content: High vitamin K content may reduce the effectiveness of anticoagulant medications.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some people may experience an allergic reaction to cabbage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled green cabbage can be served as a side dish, added to soups, stews, or salads. It pairs well with lemon juice, garlic, dill, or a drizzle of olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh cabbage in the refrigerator in a sealed bag for up to 2 weeks. Store cooked cabbage in an airtight container in the fridge for 3‑4 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Red pickled cabbage is a fermented product made from fresh red (purple) cabbage heads that undergo a brining process with salt, vinegar, sugar and spices. Fermentation preserves vitamins and gives it a characteristic tangy‑sweet flavor, making it a popular side dish and ingredient in salads, sandwiches and Asian‑style meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Red cabbage is rich in anthocyanins, pigments that give it a vivid color and act as antioxidants.
Pickling cabbage dates back to ancient Slavic and Germanic cuisines, where fermentation was a key method for long‑term vegetable storage.
During fermentation, probiotic bacteria of the Lactobacillus genus develop, supporting gut health.
Pickled red cabbage is often served as a garnish for meat, fish dishes and layered salads such as the Russian "herring under a fur coat".
In Japan a similar fermented cabbage called "tsukuna" is usually made from white cabbage; the red version is less common but gaining popularity.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Red cabbage provides over 100 mg of vitamin C per 100 g, supporting immune function and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress and may reduce the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Fermentation creates live bacteria that promote a healthy intestinal microbiome and improve digestion.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: The cabbage is a good source of fiber, helping regulate blood sugar and increase satiety.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It contains potassium, calcium and iron, important for heart, bone and blood health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Pickled cabbage contains a notable amount of salt; people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Cabbage allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cabbage or fermentation by‑products.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large portions can cause gas and bloating in those with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Quality control
items.content: Improperly fermented cabbage may harbor harmful bacteria; purchase from reputable producers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat it straight as a snack, add to salads, sandwiches, tacos, wraps and soups. It pairs well with carrots, apples, nuts and spices such as cumin or coriander. Before serving, you can gently squeeze out excess brine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep pickled cabbage refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in a sealed container. Shelf life is typically 3‑6 months. Discard if you notice off‑odors, mold or discoloration.

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken liver is a tender offal with a mild creamy flavor and a slightly earthy edge. Fresh liver has an even dark red or brownish color. Liver cooks quickly but easily dries out and turns tough. It is fried, stewed, made into pâté, and used in fillings and salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken liver is one of the richest foods in vitamin A and B12.
Liver pâté is a classic dish of French and Jewish cuisines.
Liver cooks very quickly, in just a few minutes, and turns tough if overcooked.
Before cooking, membranes and greenish areas, which can add bitterness, are removed.
Liver is often soaked in milk to soften its flavor.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A is important for vision, skin, and the immune system.

items.title: Very rich in vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is important for the nervous system and the formation of blood cells.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is important for cell formation.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from liver is well absorbed and is needed for oxygen transport.

items.title: Contains riboflavin, selenium, and choline
items.content: These nutrients support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Too much vitamin A
items.content: Liver contains a lot of retinol; during pregnancy it is usually advised to limit or avoid it, and others should not eat it too often.

items.title: Undercooked liver
items.content: Chicken liver may contain Campylobacter and Salmonella; it must be fully cooked, with no pink center.

items.title: Cholesterol and gout
items.content: Liver is high in cholesterol and purines, which are undesirable with high cholesterol and gout.

items.title: Excess iron
items.content: People with excess iron in the body should discuss liver with a doctor.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rinse the liver, remove the membranes and bile-stained areas, and if you like, soak it in milk for half an hour. Then fry over medium heat for about 5–7 minutes, or stew, until it is no longer pink inside. Liver is used for pâté, fillings, salads, and braised dishes with sour cream and onion.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Raw liver is highly perishable: keep it in the refrigerator for one to two days or freeze it. Thaw in the refrigerator. Keep cooked liver in the refrigerator for three to four days.

content.title: About
content.content: Green beans (edible pods of the common bean) are young fruits harvested at 8‑12 days of age. Raw beans have a crisp texture, a mildly sweet flavor, and a bright green color. They can be eaten fresh, added to salads and snacks, or briefly cooked for a softer bite.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green beans belong to the legume family and are closely related to peas, lentils, and soy.
Unlike mature beans, green beans are edible raw, though they are often blanched to preserve color and tenderness.
They contain more vitamin C than most other vegetables.
Traditional Asian cuisines use them in stir‑fries and salads with soy‑based dressings.
Green beans can be grown in pots, making them a popular urban‑garden vegetable.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Protein in green beans helps maintain muscle mass and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, helps regulate blood sugar, and supports gut health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Green beans are virtually fat‑free, making them suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: High in folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Food poisoning risk
items.content: Raw beans may contain small amounts of phytohemagglutinin, which can be toxic in large quantities. If the beans taste bitter or smell off, it is safer to blanch them.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to legumes and may experience skin rashes or more severe symptoms.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large servings of raw beans can cause gas and bloating due to oligosaccharides.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw green beans can be tossed into salads, blended into smoothies, dipped in hummus, or simply enjoyed as a crunchy snack. For a softer bite, blanch them for 2‑3 minutes and shock in ice water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store green beans in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. They stay fresh for 5‑7 days. Discard any wilted or damaged pods before use.

infant-formula-gerber-good-start-gentle-.title: Gerber Good Start Gentle, Stage 1, powder (350)

content.title: About
content.content: Gerber Good Start Gentle is a Stage 1 infant formula designed for newborns and babies up to 6 months. The powder is prepared with regular tap water. The formula contains partially hydrolyzed protein, prebiotics and DHA, supporting gentle digestion and brain development.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Stage 1 formula is intended for infants from birth to 6 months.
Partially hydrolyzed protein reduces the risk of allergic reactions in sensitive infants.
Prebiotics (FOS) promote a healthy gut microbiome.
DHA, derived from fish oil, is important for visual and neural development.
The formula is gluten‑free and lactose‑free, making it suitable for children with intolerances.

items.title: Supports brain development
items.content: DHA in the formula aids the formation of neural connections and visual acuity.

items.title: Easy digestion
items.content: Partially hydrolyzed protein is easier to absorb, reducing colic and constipation.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Prebiotics foster growth of beneficial bacteria, strengthening the immune system.

items.title: Balanced vitamins and minerals
items.content: The formula provides iron, calcium, vitamin D and other micronutrients essential for growth.

items.title: Gluten‑ and lactose‑free
items.content: Suitable for infants with sensitivities to these components.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Despite hydrolysis, some infants may still react to milk protein.

items.title: Improper dilution
items.content: A solution that is too concentrated can strain the kidneys; follow manufacturer instructions.

items.title: Water temperature control
items.content: Use warm (≈ 37 °C) water, not hot, to preserve nutrients.

items.title: Shelf‑life after opening
items.content: Use the opened container within 30 days and keep it in a dry place.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Mix the specified amount of powder with warm (≈ 37 °C) tap water. Stir thoroughly until smooth, avoiding lumps. The prepared feed should be used immediately.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, seal tightly and use within one month.

content.title: About
content.content: A cheese muffin is a soft baked good made from wheat flour, eggs, milk, and grated cheese. It has a gentle aroma, a slightly sweet dough flavor, and a pronounced cheesy note. Suitable for breakfast or a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cheese muffins are popular in the US and the UK, often served in cafés.
There are many variations: cheddar, mozzarella, parmesan, and even blue cheese.
The batter usually does not require a long rise, so muffins bake quickly.
Cheese in the batter increases protein content and gives a golden crust.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Cheese provides a good source of complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium from cheese supports bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic potential (when using fermented cheeses)
items.content: Some cheeses, like camembert, may contribute to a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or casein allergy may react to cheese muffins.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Cheese muffins are high in fat and calories, so they should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheese is often salty, which can be an issue for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheese muffins can be enjoyed warm straight from the oven or reheated in a microwave. They pair well with salads, soups, or as part of a brunch spread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days or in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Reheat to 180 °C before serving to restore a crisp crust.

content.title: About
content.content: Isopure is a high‑quality nutritional powder containing 100 % whey protein isolate, minimal carbs and fats, and a blend of vitamins and minerals. It is designed to support muscle recovery, maintain nutritional balance, and conveniently boost daily protein intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Isopure provides 100 % whey protein isolate, delivering over 90 % protein by weight.
The powder is lactose‑free, making it suitable for people with lactose intolerance.
Each serving contains more than 20 g of pure protein and less than 1 g of carbohydrates.
Available in several flavors such as vanilla, chocolate, and strawberry.
Isopure has undergone clinical testing confirming its effectiveness for muscle growth and recovery.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Over 20 g of protein per serving supports muscle growth and repair after workouts.

items.title: Low carbohydrate level
items.content: Less than 1 g of carbs makes it suitable for keto and low‑carb diets.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: Whey isolate is processed to remove lactose, reducing the risk of intolerance.

items.title: Fortified with vitamins and minerals
items.content: Includes B‑vitamins, vitamin C, calcium, and magnesium to support overall metabolism.

items.title: Hydration support
items.content: Easily dissolves in water, helping rapid fluid replenishment after intense exercise.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Contains whey protein, which may trigger reactions in individuals allergic to dairy proteins.

items.title: Excessive protein intake
items.content: Very high protein consumption can strain kidneys in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Some flavors contain sucralose or acesulfame‑K, which may be undesirable for sensitive users.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: High calcium and magnesium levels can affect absorption of certain drugs, such as antibiotics.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mix one scoop (≈30 g) with 250–300 ml of water, milk, or a plant‑based beverage. For extra calories and flavor, add fruit, nuts, or oats. Consume post‑workout or as a protein snack between meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the lid tightly sealed to prevent moisture ingress. Discard if clumps, off‑smell, or off‑taste develop.

content.title: About
content.content: Relish is marinated corn prepared in a traditional recipe with vinegar, spices, and a touch of sugar. The kernels stay crisp while acquiring a mildly sweet‑sour flavor characteristic of relish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Relish is a popular bar and restaurant snack, especially in the United States.
Traditional recipes use gelatin to keep the kernels firm in the jar.
Sweet, large‑kernel corn varieties are chosen for the best taste.
Some regions add smoked paprika for a subtle smoky aroma.
Properly canned relish can be stored for up to a year.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Corn provides fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in corn help protect the eyes from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many snack foods, marinated corn is low in fat.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Carbohydrates in corn quickly provide the body with energy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The brine can be high in sodium, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience an allergic reaction to corn.

items.title: Added sugar
items.content: Some recipes include sugar, increasing the product’s calorie count.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Commercially produced relish may contain preservatives that not everyone tolerates.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Relish can be enjoyed straight from the jar, added to salads, tacos, burritos, or used as a side for meat dishes. Drain excess brine before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep an opened jar of relish refrigerated and sealed with its lid. When stored properly, it remains flavorful for 2‑3 weeks. Discard if the smell or taste changes.

content.title: About
content.content: Salad Dressing Light NFS is a low‑calorie vinaigrette made from a blend of vegetable oils, vinegar, and aromatic herbs. It is designed for those watching their calorie intake without sacrificing flavor. The product contains no artificial colors or preservatives.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Reduced fat content is achieved by using a mix of canola and sunflower oils.
The formula includes a vinegar extract that gives a characteristic light tang.
The dressing is enriched with B‑group vitamins and vitamin E derived from plant ingredients.
NFS (No Fat Substitute) indicates the absence of fat replacers.
Packaging is made from recyclable plastic, reducing environmental impact.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: One tablespoon provides about 25 kcal, making it suitable for diet‑friendly meals.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Vitamin E and herb polyphenols help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The vinegar component stimulates gastric juice production, aiding nutrient absorption.

items.title: May help lower cholesterol
items.content: Plant oils containing monounsaturated fatty acids can contribute to normal LDL levels.

items.title: Enhances flavor without excess fat
items.content: Herbal aromatics boost taste, allowing a smaller amount of dressing to be used.

items.title: Allergy to vegetable oils
items.content: Some individuals may react to canola or sunflower oil.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity may irritate the stomach lining if consumed in large quantities.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The product contains moderate salt; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: The dressing is suitable for green and vegetable salads, marinating fish or chicken, and as a light base for cold sandwiches. Typically add 1–2 tablespoons per serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 2 °C–6 °C. Once opened, use within 30 days. Do not freeze. Discard if the smell or taste changes.
